title: Role-adapter reads each emit one structured audit event on the fixed allow-list
asA: operator running the runtime-verify suite against the role adapter
iWant: every read call to write one structured `keycloak.roles` event carrying only the allow-list fields
soThat: the audit stream stays free of raw claim records and every malformed-claim refusal carries a stable reasonClass

acceptanceCriteria.description: A read on a well-formed claim emits exactly one `keycloak.roles` audit event with `outcome=verified` and the caller's realmSlug.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a verified claim record whose expected role path is an array of strings, in realm `alpha`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter reads the roles from the claim record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.roles` and `outcome=verified`; no raw claim record and no token material appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A read where the expected path is present but the value is not an array of strings emits exactly one refused event with `reasonClass=malformed`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a verified claim record whose expected role path is present as a scalar value or an array of non-string values, in realm `alpha`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter reads the roles from the claim record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event with `family=keycloak.roles`, `outcome=refused`, and `reasonClass=malformed`; the raw claim record does not appear in any field; the reduced roles array is not populated

acceptanceCriteria.description: A caller whose claim record was malformed on a first read and well-formed on a second read (a claim refresh) emits exactly one refused event and one verified event on the `keycloak.roles` family, in order; the retry itself is not a distinct event.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller whose first claim read is malformed and whose second claim read (after a re-verify) is well-formed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter reads twice in sequence
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly two events in order: one `keycloak.roles` event with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=malformed`, then one `keycloak.roles` event with `outcome=verified`; no additional event is written for the retry itself

acceptanceCriteria.description: A sink failure during the emission of a `keycloak.roles` event does not mask the underlying read outcome; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and the read outcome is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a verified claim record whose expected role path is well-formed and an audit sink whose write throws
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter emits the completion event
acceptanceCriteria.then: the read's return value (the reduced roles array or the refusal) is unchanged; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event carrying the realm slug and a reason-class string; the raw claim record does not appear in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: Reading roles twice from the same well-formed verified claim record is idempotent: each read emits exactly one `keycloak.roles` audit event with `outcome=verified`; two consecutive reads produce two events (count is one per read call).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a verified claim record whose expected role path is an array of strings in realm `alpha`, and one completed read already on record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter reads the roles from the same claim record a second time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one additional event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.roles` and `outcome=verified`; the total count of `keycloak.roles` verified events across the two reads is exactly two; the reduced roles array returned by the second read is identical to the first

acceptanceCriteria.description: A read on a claim record whose expected role path is absent (the caller's credential carries no granted role and so no operation is permitted through this mechanism) emits exactly one `keycloak.roles` audit event with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=roles_absent`; the reduced roles array is not populated and no operation is authorised downstream.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a verified claim record in realm `alpha` whose expected role path is not present on the record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the role adapter reads the roles from the claim record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, reasonClass, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.roles`, `outcome=refused`, and `reasonClass=roles_absent`; the raw claim record does not appear in any field; the reduced roles array is not populated

description: Applying agent sets: no project-parameterised values on this story; every AC is `fixed`. AC-set sufficiency (7a inline note per blueprint-authoring.md §7a): the credential scenario class is bound by AC-1 (a verified claim record is the credential and the event records the realm-scoped identity via the `realmSlug` payload field). The permission scenario class is bound by AC-6 (a claim record whose expected role path is absent carries no granted role, so the mechanism refuses with `reasonClass=roles_absent` and populates no reduced roles array).
